resources.string: Opens RustDesk so %1$s can see your phone.
A wide button that fetches help

HANDYHelfer knows exactly one person who may help. That is deliberate: if someone calls claiming to be from a company, they cannot talk you into entering a different number — there is no field for one.
This number cannot be called. Please check it again.
This is when help was requested. The list stays on this phone and cannot be deleted.
RustDesk must be installed before anyone can see your screen. It is not in the Play Store — shall I open its download page?
HANDYHelfer is not allowed to place calls itself. The number is now in the phone app — tap Call there.
Airplane mode is on. Calls cannot get through.
The phone is silenced. You will not hear it ring.
The ringer is set to %1$s out of %2$s. That is easy to miss.
“Do not disturb” is on. Calls stay silent.
Storage is nearly full, only %1$s MB left. Updates will fail.
Storage is getting tight, %1$s MB left.
Battery saver is on. It shuts down apps in the background.
No restart for %1$s days. A lot of problems solve themselves that way.
Text size is set very large. Some apps then cut off their buttons.
Android %1$s no longer receives security updates.
RustDesk is not installed. Without it nobody can look at the screen.

What is this for?

A button that fetches help. You tap it, and the person you chose gets a call.

And how do they see my phone?

That is what RustDesk is for, a separate program. The second button opens it. Your helper only sees your screen once you agree on the phone — Android demands that for every session, and nobody can get around it.

Why can I only enter one person?

Because that is the protection. There are callers who pose as company staff and try to talk you into entering a different number. HANDYHelfer has no field for that. Anyone who wanted to would first have to explain how to open the setup screen — and that is the point to hang up.

What does my helper see of me?

Only what is on the screen, and only while you have agreed. HANDYHelfer itself sends nothing anywhere: the status report on the home screen is displayed, not transmitted. Your helper reads it when looking at the screen.

Who was connected, and when?

That is in the log. It stays on this phone and cannot be deleted from within the app.
